chapter: Hampton, Andy Kirk and Charlie Barnet
title: Run-ins with Barnet; hanging out with Prez
summary: He criticised Barnet's playing, then recalls staying out all night with Lester Young while Basie was at the Lincoln.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Yeah, so like we said... We had a couple of run-ins... Charlie and I had a couple of run-ins one time, where I told him... I said, "Well, you can't play shit anyway" -- which he got mad at the time. But he was good for what he was trying to do. Like, I liked him for what he was trying to do.
No, he was never a great soloist.
No, he wasn't. He didn't play that hot, you know what I mean. I mean, he wasn't no Lester Young.
Lester Young, man, that was the shit. Boy, I said "Goddamn..." I used go hang out with Prez at... We was here at the Capitol Theatre, like I said, and we were...

Basie was at the Lincoln. And I'd hang out with Prez all night long, and come into the theatre at ten o'clock in the morning, and couldn't hardly see straight, I'd be so damn tired. But I'd do that, and make that first show with Charlie. It doesn't matter. You go back on out there with Prez, and listen to him play again. Oh, he would play so pretty, man. I just couldn't stand not being around him, and hanging out in New York, too...
